contract: Construct a length-prefixed NAL reader for each sample and provide windows of 1, 7 or 4,096 bytes. Read the sample length fields independently on the reference side. Feed each complete unit to a fresh AVC or HEVC MP4-to-Annex-B filter with empty configuration arrays and the same length width. An incomplete suffix refuses after the complete input units; if a zero length leaves a suffix, submit that invalid suffix to the filter as one span. Script packet metadata and side data are outside this comparison.

Remove the start code or length field and compare all units in source order. Fold kind 1 with sample and unit index, sample-relative payload offset, unit type, AVC ref idc and zero or HEVC layer id and temporal id plus one, and length and bytes, including the original header. The reference uses the physical offsets of the length-delimited units and removes only the single leading start code from each returned unit. Fold kind 7 with sample index and unit count or kind 8 with sample index on refusal.
Loading and script parsing are outside the operation. Reader setup, window feeding, reference Annex B conversion and prefix removal, ordered folding and teardown are inside.

open_deviations.reading: A sample NAL length cannot be zero
open_deviations.clause: ISO/IEC 14496-15 NAL-unit sample carriage, as documented by NalReader; ITU-T H.264 clause 7.3.1 defines the mandatory one-byte NAL header
open_deviations.candidate: emits any complete units up to the zero length and refuses the empty declared unit
open_deviations.reference: skips the zero-length AVC unit and reports clean end
